note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. Six of seven regular members were present (Brooke Reed absent); one student representative attended (the other graduated with the Class of 2026 days earlier). A largely ceremonial meeting honoring Teachers of the Year and retirees; every vote passed unanimously. Summarization necessarily condenses and selects; for complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Chair Andrea Mancuso, Vice Chair Katy Rice, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Dr. Flynn Ross. Absent: Brooke Reed.

blocks.x: Recognition: Teachers of the Year & Retirees

One honoree per building: Michael Crawford (physical education, Westbrook Middle School), Haley Tardiff (special education, Sacarappa School), Selena Mardin (kindergarten, Congin Elementary School), Kirk Nigren (building trades, Westbrook Regional Vocational Center (WRVC)), Brian Adams (math, Westbrook High School), and Hannah Gundersdorf (kindergarten, Canal School).

Eric Jensen (7 years, Transportation; Jody Peterson was also honored from Transportation, with Melissa Foy accepting on Peterson's behalf), Sandy Beasley (37 years, Canal), a Westbrook Middle School staff member with 39 years of service (name not clearly captured in the transcript), Maura McDermott (5 years, special education, Westbrook Middle School), Juni Dugas (25 years, administrative assistant, Westbrook Middle School), Paula Curcio (35 years, social studies, Westbrook Middle School), Marina Davis (7 years, math, Westbrook High School), Sarah Barker (cook, Westbrook High School), Nicole Sturgis (10 years, aspirations counselor, Westbrook High School), and Wendy Harvey (12 years, co-principal, Westbrook High School).
The fiscal year 2027 (FY27) school budget referendum passed with roughly 70% voting yes. Superintendent Lancia thanked voters, administrators, and committee members.

The Class of 2026 graduated the prior Saturday. Over $500,000 in scholarships were awarded at Class Night. Another roughly $62,000–$65,000 in scholarships/toolships was awarded at WRVC's awards night. An Adult Education graduation was also held.

2026–27 calendar: no staggered start. Grades 1–12 begin Monday, August 31. Kindergarten begins Wednesday, September 2. Pre-K opens Thursday, September 3. The staff back-to-school luncheon is Friday, August 28.

Special services leadership restructuring: Director of Special Services Kelly Fogg retired last year. Repeated searches for a replacement, including one this year, were unsuccessful. Fogg has worked this year as a 3-day-a-week contracted consultant. Dr. Lancia proposed keeping two full-time assistant directors. One is fully funded by the general fund. The other is funded 20% by the general fund and 80% by the Maine Department of Education. That split reflects that position's oversight of pre-K special education and “child find” requirements. Lancia also proposed adding a third assistant director for one year only. That job would be paid for by the savings from not filling the director position, plus an increased state funding share. There would be no new general-fund money. Fogg would continue as a paid consultant. Asked by Noreen Poitras in discussion, Lancia said the new position would be a one-year-only bargaining-unit contract (a contract for employees a union represents). It would be reassessed before the FY28 budget. Poitras also asked for full salary and structure details. Asked by Mancuso, Lancia said the savings should entirely cover the position (aside from possible benefits costs). He also said no board action was needed, since no new money was involved. Lancia explained that the special education director role is difficult to fill statewide. He cited its specific certification requirements and small candidate pools. He said partnering with a neighboring district's director has not been explored, given Westbrook's position as the county's largest special education program. He remains open to it.
Spring Assessment Data — Dr. Kim O'Donnell

Dr. O'Donnell also announced she is leaving after six years for Scarborough Public Schools. She presented Northwest Evaluation Association growth and achievement data comparing 2024–25 to 2025–26 across grades K–10. The data showed generally stable-to-improving trends districtwide. Westbrook High School had 60% or better of students meeting growth targets. Westbrook Middle School was close to 60%. The elementary schools were generally positive, with some dips (notably in Sacarappa achievement). In response to questions from Cavallaro, she distinguished “achievement” (performance against grade-level expectation) from “growth target” (predicted year-over-year progress). She also said district benchmarking data could be pulled with more lead time.

Thanked outgoing senior student representative Tina for her service, having just watched her graduate. Welcomed Jamila Mohamed Ahmed, who continues into her third year as student representative. Noted unusually high turnout for a June vote. Thanked staff, the City Hall elections team, and City Clerk Ledoux, whose official results came a little after 2 a.m.

Shared a parent message praising Congin Elementary principal Mark Bisson's leadership. Tied it to the achievement gains just presented. (Congin raised math and reading proficiency by nearly 12% over two years. It served a growing share of students in poverty and with disabilities.)

Reported ongoing conversations with City staff about pesticide/fertilizer use on shared school/municipal athletic fields. These included an informal meeting with City Administrator Angela Holmes and Mayor David Morse. Field-maintenance contracts have not been rebid in some time. Mancuso's sense was that the City hopes to gather information over the summer. Then requests for proposals (formal calls for vendors to bid) that account for the school department's field needs can go out in the fall. She will share her notes with Dr. Lancia and the committee.
Student Representative Report — Jamila Mohamed Ahmed

The end of the year is winding down districtwide. Events include step-up and field days at the elementary and middle schools. There is a district-wide 4th grade Beach Day sponsored by the Westbrook Education Foundation. Sacarappa has an end-of-year picnic and field day. Westbrook Middle School's 8th grade promotion is June 16, with a dance after. The last day of school is June 17. Congin has a Parent Teacher Organization family fun night. Westbrook High School has finals.

Policy (Cavallaro) and Educational Programs (Rice): no meetings in May. Finance (Poitras): no update. Facilities (reported by Dr. Lancia in Brooke Reed's absence): the committee toured Sacarappa School in May, including the roof where the school's solar panels are installed and generating power.
11.1–11.5 — Final Approval of Five Items Held Over From First Approval (Taken in the Aggregate)

Policy JICJ (student device use/cell-phone ban), Policy EEA (student transportation), Policy IKB (homework), the Maine Learning Technology Initiative (MLTI) purchase for 2026–2027, and the Yonder pouch fund reallocation.

Notably, JICJ and the Yonder pouch funding had each split 5–1 at first approval on May 13. Noreen Poitras cast both dissents (on JICJ, on student-safety grounds). At final approval, Poitras herself moved this aggregate motion, which included both items.
Approved 6–0 by show of hands (Reed not yet present), moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Katy Rice.
12.1 — Ten Administrator/Teacher Nominations (Taken in the Aggregate), First and Final Approval

Nurse (elementary school, building name unclear in the transcript), Kindergarten Teacher (Sacarappa), two Pre-Kindergarten Teachers (Canal), Grade 3 Teacher (Sacarappa), Grade 2 Teacher (Canal), Social Studies Teacher (Westbrook High School), a Special Education Teacher (Westbrook High School), School Counselor (Westbrook High School), and Career Readiness School Counselor (Westbrook High School).
Approved 6–0, moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Erin Cavallaro.
12.2 — Superintendent's Summer Hiring-Decision Waiver, First and Final Approval

Allows Dr. Lancia to hire teachers over the summer without waiting for committee nomination (hires reported at the next meeting). Lancia clarified a packet typo: the waiver covers teacher hires only, not administrators.
Approved 6–0, moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
12.3 — Hire an Additional Pre-K General Education Teacher and Pre-K Ed Tech, First and Final Approval

In response to a question from Dr. Flynn Ross, Dr. Lancia confirmed this is driven by enrollment demand. The pre-K program is expanding to three classrooms/six sessions (three teachers, three ed techs). It already has 74 students enrolled, with a week still remaining before the deadline. Canal School is now at its space maximum. More enrollment brings more state subsidy through the October 1 count.
Approved 6–0, moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Allison Brunette.

June 17: last day of school (half day). August 5, 5:00 PM: Finance Committee (Central Office). August 12, 7:00 PM: next regular School Committee meeting (Room 114, Westbrook High School). August 31: first day of school.
Recess Into Executive Session — Personnel Matter
Under 1 Maine Revised Statutes Annotated §405(6)(A) (personnel matters). An executive session is a closed, private session allowed by state law for certain topics.
The chair announced a change to the agenda order at the start of the meeting. The committee adjourned directly from executive session with no further public action.
Approved 6–0, moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
